description: Authoritative scientific thresholds, guideline limits, and scoring parameters for BQAS.

sugars.name: Free sugars
sugars.rationale: WHO conditionally recommends reducing free sugars intake to below 5% of total energy (approx. 25 g/day for a 2,000 kcal diet) for lifelong health benefits, with a strong recommendation to remain below 10% (50 g/day).

caffeine.name: Caffeine
caffeine.source_organization: European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) / US FDA
caffeine.rationale: EFSA Scientific Opinion establishes 200 mg single dose for adults (approx. 3 mg/kg) and 400 mg daily as not raising safety concerns for healthy adults. In pregnancy, daily intake must remain below 200 mg. For children and adolescents, safe level is 3 mg/kg body weight per day.

sodium_benzoate.name: Sodium benzoate (E211)
sodium_benzoate.rationale: Group Acceptable Daily Intake (ADI) of 5 mg/kg body weight per day expressed as benzoic acid.

sulphites.name: Sulphites (as SO2)
sulphites.rationale: Group ADI of 0.7 mg/kg body weight per day expressed as sulfur dioxide equivalent.

alcohol.name: Alcohol
alcohol.who_statement: According to the World Health Organization (2023), there is no evidence of a threshold at which the carcinogenic and health risks of alcohol consumption are absent. No level of alcohol consumption is completely safe for health.
alcohol.source_organization: World Health Organization (WHO) Regional Office for Europe
alcohol.rationale: Alcohol is a toxic, psychoactive, and Group 1 carcinogenic substance causally linked to 7 types of cancer.

methanol.name: Methanol
methanol.display_unit: g per L of pure alcohol
methanol.source_organization: EU Spirit Drinks Regulations / Toxicology Literature
methanol.rationale: Methanol is metabolised into toxic formaldehyde and formic acid, causing metabolic acidosis and blindness. Strict legal maximums apply to distilled spirits (~10 g/L pure ethanol in fruit spirits).

sodium.name: Sodium
sodium.rationale: WHO recommends adults consume less than 2,000 mg of sodium per day (equivalent to 5 g of salt) to reduce blood pressure and risk of cardiovascular disease.

taurine.name: Taurine
taurine.rationale: Customary level in energy drinks (~4,000 mg/L) concluded by EFSA to not pose safety concerns for healthy consumers.
